To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ALFWorld, an embodied simulator for learning from text and executing goals in a visual environment, enables agents to generalize better than training only in visual environments; ALFWorld enables researchers to focus on the individual components that make an embodied agent effective.

1) ALFWorld provides a flexible, modular platform that enables researchers to develop and compare models for embodied agents that reason abstractly and execute concretely; and 2) BUTLER, trained on ALFWorld, achieves the highest success rates of any model on ALFRED to date, demonstrating the value of abstract reasoning for embodied agents.

1) ALFWorld provides a new simulator for training agents to perform embodied tasks, 2) BUTLER, a simple agent that learns to perform these tasks, demonstrates the potential of this approach, and 3) ALFWorld enables researchers to study every piece of the embodied AI pipeline.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how embodied agents learn to act in complex visual environments.
how to best combine abstract and concrete knowledge to improve the generalization and robustness of embodied agents.

the following questions: 1) Can we learn a general, abstract policy in a text-based environment that can be transferred to the visual domain? 2) Can we learn abstract knowledge that can be executed in both text and visual domains? 3) Can we learn to execute goals in the visual domain using an abstract policy?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ALFWorld provides a platform for studying the interaction between abstract and embodied agents.

the paper introduces the ALFWorld simulator, a new benchmark that enables the training of embodied agents in two environments: a text-based environment (TextWorld) and a visually grounded one (ALFRED).
ALFWorld is a simulator that enables embodied agents to learn abstract text-based policies and execute goals from the rich ALFRED benchmark in a visual environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are introducing a simulator for embodied agents that allows for the transfer of knowledge from text-based environments to visually grounded ones, and we provide a modular architecture for embodied agents.
we introduce ALFWorld, an interactive environment that enables agents to plan abstractly in text and execute concretely in a visually grounded setting.

we have created a simulator to enable embodied learning from language, which we hope will be used by the community to develop agents that can learn to understand and execute instructions from natural language.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ALFWorld simulator provides an important stepping stone for the development of embodied agents that can reason in abstract terms and then execute their plans in the real world.
the combination of a text-based environment for abstract planning with a rich visual environment for concrete action is a powerful tool for advancing embodied intelligence.
the ALFWorld simulator can be used to develop and evaluate embodied, multi-modal agents with the potential to learn from text, images, and videos.
